text: ἀγαπάω, I love (never of love between the sexes, but nearly always of the love of (the) God or (the) Christ to us, and of our love to Him and to our fellow creatures, as inspired by His love for us).

ἀγάπη (a word exclusively Biblical, curtailed from ἀγάπησις [from ἀγαπάω]: in LXX generally of sexual love; first in higher sense not before about 100 B.C.), love [this was the sense of the word charity in the time of the A.V.], as that of (the) God or (the) Christ to us, and our love to Him and to our fellow creatures thus inspired: ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦ χριστοῦ are sometimes ambiguous, when it is doubtful whether (the) God's, (the) Christ's love for us, or our love for (the) God, (the) Christ, is intended; in most cases the former is probably the primary thought: ἀγάπαι plur. (Jude, verse 12) concr., of the love-feasts of the Christians, evening meals partaken of by Christians in the early Church, either accompanied or followed by the Eucharist. Such common meals were sacred, and intended to be expressive of the union of Christians in their Head.

ἀγαθός, (intrinsically) good, good (in nature), good (whether it be seen to be so or not), the widest and most colourless of all words with this meaning (opp. πονηρός, κακός): τὰ ἀγαθά (bona), the goods, Lk. xii 18.
ἀγαλλιάω, I exult, I am full of joy.

ἅγιος, set apart by (or for) the God, holy, sacred, e.g. ἁγία πόλις (of Jerusalem) Mt. iv 5; τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, practically synonymous with τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ (Mk. i 24) of the Messiah; οἱ ἅγιοι, of the Christians as the new people of God, taking the place of the Hebrews: τὸ ἅγιον, τὰ ἅγια, the temple; τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, the inmost part of the temple, the inner shrine.
ἄγγελος, a messenger, generally: a (supernatural) messenger from God, an angel, conveying news or behests from (the) God to men: almost an intermediary, Gal. iii 19.

ἀγαπητός, loved, beloved, with two special applications, (a) ὁ ἀγαπητός, the Beloved, a title of the Messiah (Christ), as beloved beyond all others by the God who sent Him; (b) of Christians, as beloved by God, Christ, and one another.
ἁγιάζω (apparently exclusively Biblical), I make ἅγιος, treat as ἅγιος (set apart, holy), sanctify, hallow (see ἅγιος).
ἁγιασμός, the process of making or becoming ἅγιος (set apart, holy).
ἀγοράζω, I buy.
ἀγνοέω, I do not know, I am ignorant of (a person, thing, or fact), sometimes with the idea of wilful ignorance.
ἀγορά, market-place, market.
ἁγνός (originally, in a condition prepared for worship), pure (either ethically, or ritually, ceremonially); chaste.
ἁγνίζω, I make pure, either (a) ceremonially (e.g. Ac. xxi 24), or (b) actually (e.g. 1 Pet. i 22).

ἄγω, (a) I lead, I lead away, I bring (a person, or animal); thus I bring before a court of justice; (b) especially in 1st pers. plur. subjunct. ἄγωμεν, intr. let us depart (e.g. Mk. i 38); (c) I hold, keep, celebrate: ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται (Ac. xix 38), assizes are held.
ἀγρός (a word rare in papyrus documents, and now obsolete), a field, especially as bearing a crop; the country, Mk. xv 21, xvi 12: plur. ἀγροί, lands, property in land, a country estate.
ἀγών, an (athletic) contest; hence, a struggle (in the soul).

ἀδελφός, (a) a brother (so probably even in Rom. xvi 23, 2 Cor. xii 18); (b) (a use characteristic of Jewish literature but not confined to it) a member of the same religious community, especially a fellow-Christian (particularly in the plural).
ἀδικέω, I act unjustly towards, I injure, I harm (animate or inanimate).
ἀδελφή, (a) a sister; (b) a woman (fellow-)member of a church, a Christian woman (Rom. xvi 1; 1 Cor. vii 15, &c.).
ἀδικία, injustice, unrighteousness, hurt; sometimes in a Hebraistic genitive, equivalent to the adjective ἄδικος (e.g. Lk. xvi 8, xviii 6).
ἄδικος, unjust, unrighteous (opp. δίκαιος).
ᾅδης (in LXX=Sheol), Hades, the unseen world, into which the spirits of all persons pass at death.
ἀθετέω, I annul, make of no effect, set aside, ignore, slight; I break faith with, Mk. vi 26.
ἀδύνατος, (a) of persons, incapable (Ac. xiv 8, Rom. xv 1); (b) of things, impossible; τὸ ἀδύνατον, either the inability, or that which is impossible (Rom. viii 3).
ἀδόκιμος, failing to pass the test, unapproved, counterfeit.
αἴρω, (a) I raise, lift up; (b) I take away, remove.
αἷμα, blood (especially as shed): σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα (αἷμα καὶ σὰρξ), a Hebraistic expression for a human being, human beings, human nature.

αἰών (from a root meaning life, especially long life, old age), an age, a cycle (of time), especially of the present age as contrasted with the future age, and of one of a series of ages stretching to infinity: ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος, from the beginning of the present age, from the beginning of time, Lk. i 70, &c.: εἰς αἰῶνα (in saeculum, in aeternum, Ambros. expos. ps. cxviii 12 7 § 1): αἰῶνες αἰώνων, a Hebraistic expression, more emphatic than the simple αἰῶνες Gal. i 5, &c.
αἰτέω, I ask, request, beg, petition: middle voice αἰτέομαι, I ask for myself (perhaps with entreaty).
αἰώνιος, (a) age-long, and, therefore, practically eternal, unending; (b) partaking of the character of that which lasts for an age, as contrasted with that which is brief and fleeting.
αἰτία, (a) a cause, reason; excuse; (b) a charge, accusation; (c) guilt; (d) relationship, matter, circumstances, case (= causa), Mt. xix 10.
ἀκολουθέω (takes the place of the old ἕπομαι), I accompany, attend.
ἀκάθαρτος, unclean, impure: in reference to demons, spirits, Mt. x 1, &c.
ἀκοή, (a) hearing, faculty of hearing; ear: in ἀκοῇ ἀκούειν (Mt. xiii 14, &c.), a Hebraistic (?) expression, the ἀκοῇ is emphatic; (b) report, rumour.
ἄκανθα, a thorn-bush.
ἀκαθαρσία, uncleanness, impurity.
ἀκαταστασία, disturbance, upheaval, revolution, almost anarchy, first in the political, and thence in the moral sphere.
ἀκούω, I hear, listen; in the passive, is heard, is reported: ἀκοῇ ἀκούειν, see ἀκοή.
ἀκροβυστία (a technical word of Jewish use, adapted from ἀκροποσθία [?]), foreskin, prepuce: used sometimes as a slang term by Jews, of Gentiles (Eph. ii 11).
ἀλήθεια, truth, but not merely truth as spoken; truth of idea, reality, sincerity, truth in the moral sphere, straightforwardness: ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας, really, truly.
ἀληθινός (less common than ἀληθής), true (lit. made of truth), real, genuine.
ἀληθής, true in fact; hence more widely (see ἀλήθεια).
ἀληθῶς, truly, verily.
ἀλέκτωρ, a cock.
ἀλλά (used very like πλήν), but; except, Mk. iv 22, Mt. xx 23; ἀλλ᾽ ἤ, except, 2 Cor. i 13; in Mk. vi 9 ἀλλά is probably a misrendering of an Aramaic word meaning and not.
ἄλλος (alius), other, another (of more than two), different; see under ἕτερος; ὁ ἄλλος, the other (of two only), Mt. v 39, &c.; ἄλλοι ἄλλο τι . . . some—one thing, some—another thing.
ἀλλήλων &c. (a reciprocal word = inter se, in uicem), one another.
ἀλλότριος (alienus), belonging to another person, belonging to others.
ἀλλάσσω (transitive), I change, alter.
ἁμαρτία (error, a wrong state of mind or soul), a sin.
ἁμαρτωλός, (a) sinning, sinful; (b) frequent as a translation of a contemptuous Aramaic word, with reference to particular classes despised by strict Jews, a sinner.

ἁμαρτάνω, originally, I miss the mark; hence, (a) I make a mistake; (b) I sin, I commit a sin (against God); sometimes (Lk. xvii 4, Ac. xxv 8, &c.) the idea of sinning against a fellow-creature is present.
ἅλυσις, a (light) chain.
ἅμα, (a) adv. at the same time, therewith; (b) prep. along with, together with.
ἁμάρτημα (erratum), a fault, a sin.
ἀμήν (Hebr.), verily, truly: at the end of sentences may be paraphrased by So let it be!
ἀμπελών, a vineyard (-ών [=Lat. -etum] indicates ‘plantation of’, cf. ἐλαιών).
ἀμφότεροι, both (of two): in Ac. xix 16, xxiii 8, perhaps = all (of more than two); so in common speech and in Byzantine Greek.

ἄν, (a) an untranslatable word (under the circumstances, in that case, anyhow), the general effect of which is to make a statement contingent, which would otherwise be definite: it is thus regularly used with the subjunctive mood: cf. ἕως ἄν, until such time as, ὃς ἄν, ὅστις ἄν, whosoever, ὅσοι ἄν, as many as . . . may, ὅπως ἄν, ὡς ἄν (1 Cor. xi 34, &c., not in 1 Cor. xii 2), that so; so, with the indicative past, in the apodosis of a conditional sentence, e.g. Mt. xi 21 ἂν . . . μετένοησαν, ‘would have repented’, where μετένοησαν alone would have meant ‘repented’; cf. also Mk. vii 11 (reading ὃ ἂν . . . ὠφελήθης); and with the optative (rare in N.T.), e.g. τί ἂν θέλοι, ‘how he would like’ (Lk. i 62), where τί θέλοι would be ‘how he might like’; (b) if (=Attic ἤν, ἐάν), e.g. John xii 32 (v.l.), xiii 20.
note: μετένοησαν (twice) is accented thus on the page; transcribed as printed

text: ἀνά, prep. up; hence up along; ἀνὰ μέσον, in the middle: most commonly with a distributive force, e.g. ἀνὰ δηνάριον (Mt. xx 9), ‘a denarius each’, ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας (Lk. ix 3), ‘two tunics each’, ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα (Lk. ix 14), ‘in fifties’, ‘in groups of fifty’, ἀνὰ δύο (Lk. x 1), ‘two by two’ (where perhaps ἀνὰ δύο δύο, a mixed distributive, ought to be read).
ἀναβαίνω, I go up, mount, ascend.
ἀναγινώσκω, I read aloud (in the scriptures, i.e. the Old Testament).
ἀναβλέπω, (a) I look up, e.g. Mt. xiv 19; (b) I recover my sight, e.g. Mt. xi 5.
ἀνάγω, (a) I lead up; (b) mid. and pass. I put to sea, set sail.
ἀνάγκη, necessity, constraint, compulsion; ἔχω ἀνάγκην, I am obliged.
ἀναγγέλλω, I announce, report.
ἀναιρέω, (a) I take up, e.g. Ac. vii 21; more often (b) I take away the life of, murder (2 Thess. ii 8, text doubtful).
ἀνάκειμαι, I recline (especially at a dinner-table).
ἀνάθεμα (properly, a devoting to the vengeance of the infernal goddesses), a curse, a cursed thing. Distinguish from ἀνάθημα, q.v.
ἀνακρίνω, I examine, inquire into (judicially: see ἀνάκρισις); of the preliminary examination, preceding the trial proper: hence with derived applications.
ἀναλαμβάνω, (a) I take up, raise; (b) I pick up, 2 Tim. iv 11, or take on board, Ac. xx 13, 14; (c) I carry off, lead away, Ac. xxiii 31.
ἀναμιμνῄσκω, (a) act. I remind; (b) mid. or pass. I am reminded, remind myself, remember, recall.
ἀνάστασις, a rising again, resurrection.
ἀναπίπτω, I lie down, recline (at a dinner-table), I fall back upon (the breast of another person reclining at dinner).
ἀναπαύω, (a) act. I make to rest, I give rest to; (b) mid. and pass. I rest, take my ease (see ἀνάπαυσις).
ἀναπληρόω, (a) I fill up, make up, complete the measure of, Phil. ii 30; (b) I fulfil, I carry out the commands (provisions, &c.) of, Mt. xiii 14, Gal. vi 2, &c.
ἀναχωρέω, (a) I return, Mt. ii 12; (b) I retire, depart (underlying idea perhaps of taking refuge from danger or of going into retirement).
ἀναστροφή (conuersatio) (not in papyri, common in inscriptions), dealing with other men, going up and down among men, life, manner of life.
ἀνατολή, (a) rising of the sun; hence, (b) (sing. and plur.) the quarter whence the sun rises, the East.

ἀναστρέφω, (a) I overturn, turn upside down, John ii 15 (text doubtful); (b) I return, Ac. v 22, xv 16 (in a Hebraistic idiom, where the verb means little more than the adverb again); (c) mid. and pass. (conuersari) I conduct (behave) myself, live (with reference to the manner of life, especially in a moral and religious aspect), Mt. xvii 22 (text doubtful), &c., often with ἐν and a noun indicating condition or circumstances.
ἀναφέρω, (a) I carry up, lead up; (b) I offer up (on a high altar) as a sacrifice, I offer up to God on high.

ἄνεμος, wind (literally, and in Eph. iv 14 metaph.): in the sense quarter of the heaven, cardinal point, as both Greeks and Romans habitually defined the quarters of the heaven by the winds which came from those quarters, Mt. xxiv 31 (Mk. xiii 27).
ἀνέγκλητος, irreproachable (especially in private life), blameless.
ἀνεκτός, endurable, tolerable.
ἄνεσις (opposite of θλῖψις, lit. loosening, relaxing), (a) relief, remission, indulgence, freedom, Ac. xxiv 23; (b) rest.

ἄνθρωπος, a human being: υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου, notable because of the singular (rather than the plural ἀνθρώπων), a Hebraistic expression of a somewhat frequent type (see under υἱός), indicating a human being with all the characteristics of a human being (ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, a Messianic title especially favoured by our Lord for this very reason).
ἀνήρ (uir), a male human being, a man (contrast ἄνθρωπος); often in addresses, at the beginning of speeches = Gentlemen; a husband.
ἀνέχομαι, I endure (in 2 Thess. i 4, and Mt. vi 24=Lk. xvi 13, text doubtful).
ἀνθίστημι, only in intransitive tenses of active, and in all tenses of the middle or passive, I take a stand against, oppose, resist.
ἀνθρώπινος, belonging to human beings (especially as contrasted with God), human (as contrasted with divine): perhaps moderate, Rom. vi 19, 1 Cor. x 13.

ἀνίστημι, I raise up, set up: only the fut. ἀναστήσω and the 1 aor. ἀνέστησα are used in this transitive sense in the N.T.; much more frequent are the middle voice and the 2 aor. of the active in the intr. sense I rise, especially ἐκ νεκρῶν, from among (the) dead bodies, dead persons, the dead.
ἀνοίγω, I open.
ἀνομία, lawlessness; especially disobedience to the divine law, sin.

ἀντί (originally local, in front of, opposite), (a) instead of, in return for, in exchange for, as a substitute for; λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν Mk. x 45 (=Mt. xx 28), a ransom to buy the many, for the many; cf. Heb. xii 16 and ἀντίλυτρον; (b) ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ, on my behalf, Mt. xvii 27; (c) ἀνθ᾽ ὧν (literally, in return for which things) has become a conjunction, wherefore, because.
ἄνομος, lawless, disobedient to the law of God, sinful; illegal: ἄνομος θεοῦ=ἄνευ νόμου θεοῦ, 1 Cor. ix 21.
ἀντίκειμαι (used as a passive for ἀντιτίθημι, just as κεῖμαι is a passive for τίθημι), I resist, oppose.
ἀνταποδίδωμι, I give in return.
ἀντίδικος (aduersarius), an opponent (in a lawsuit): probably so even in 1 Pet. v 8.
